blocks.content: A named volume is a volume you explicitly create and reference by a memorable name, fully managed by Docker, and easy to reuse across containers.
docker volume create makes a new, empty, named volume, entirely managed by Docker, you never need to know or care about the exact filesystem path it lives at on the host.

blocks.alt: A named, Docker-managed piece of storage

blocks.content: Once created (or even without pre-creating it, Docker will create it automatically on first use), a named volume is mounted into a container with -v name:/path, readable and writable exactly like any other directory from inside the container.

blocks.alt: Mounted into a container just by referencing its name

blocks.content: 3. Reusing the Same Volume Across Containers
blocks.text: 3. Reusing the Same Volume Across Containers

blocks.content: Because it is addressed by a stable name, the exact same volume can be mounted into a completely different container later, deliberately, this is the mechanism behind recreating a stateful container without losing its data.

blocks.alt: The same name, mounted into a different container later

blocks.content: docker volume inspect shows the volume's actual details, including the real path on the host where Docker is storing its data underneath, useful for backups or direct inspection when something needs debugging at the filesystem level.

blocks.alt: The details Docker is managing on your behalf

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Named volumes are explicitly created, memorably named, and fully managed by Docker, the standard choice for persistent application data.
The same named volume can be mounted into a new container later, which is exactly how stateful containers get safely recreated.
